items.criterion: Identifies Directive 2002/58/EC, especially Articles 2(f) and 5(3), as the central cookie rule.
Recovers that consent requires an active, freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous indication or clear affirmative action, with legally relevant support from Directive 95/46/EC and/or GDPR.
Concludes, with retrieved support rather than recalled case law, that a preselected checkbox requiring deselection is not valid consent.
Recognizes that the ePrivacy storage/access rule does not turn on whether the information is personal data.
Identifies cookie duration as part of the information required in the circumstances.
Identifies possible third-party access or recipients as part of the information required in the circumstances.
Distinguishes the earlier Directive 95/46/EC period from possible GDPR relevance to future conduct and avoids asserting national temporal application without support.
Does not purport to resolve whether conditioning lottery participation on advertising consent was freely given when retrieved material cannot establish that unasked issue.
Every substantive legal proposition is linked to retrieved evidence; no hallucinated decisive rule is introduced.
The final analysis points in the same legal direction as the held-out ruling without overstating that it is deciding the national action.

evaluation_notes.priority: Reasoning, support, provenance and uncertainty outweigh bare outcome agreement.
